factChecks.claim: Duolingo redesigned streak milestones and sharing after user research.
Visible, celebratory progress can make effort feel worth protecting.

shareValue: A three-question test for making progress visible and worth celebrating.
caption: Duolingo turned a number into something learners protect, celebrate, and share.

slides.text: Duolingo turned a number into something people protect.
The streak makes invisible effort visible.
slides.kicker: A few minutes of daily practice becomes a number that remembers yesterday.

slides.text: But progress alone was not enough.
slides.kicker: Duolingo says research showed some new learners did not understand the streak, and milestone moments needed to feel more exciting.

slides.text: The lesson is not “add a streak.”
slides.kicker: Make real effort visible, understandable, and emotionally worth returning to.

captions.instagram:
Duolingo turned a number into something learners protect.

The streak makes small daily effort visible. But Duolingo's own design write-up shows the deeper work: make the symbol understandable, make milestones feel celebratory, and make achievements easy to share.

The takeaway is not to paste a streak onto every product. It is to give genuine progress a visible story. Save the final slide for your next retention review.

What progress does your product currently leave invisible?

Source: Duolingo, Animating the Duolingo Streak (2021)
https://blog.duolingo.com/streak-milestone-design-animation/
